subject: I am not able to Load INLA package because the foreach and doMC packages cannot be installed/loaded. Help

messages.author: 6205e4b1a72b2445
messages.subject: I am not able to Load INLA package because the foreach and doMC packages cannot be installed/loaded. Help
parts:
I am a Windows user.

Very new INLA user, but excited to try out. I downloaded the package fine, but when I was trying to run the very first example from the SPDE book, using library(INLA), I got the error saying that the package "foreach" could not be loaded, thought installing 'foreach" using install.packages() went through without a problem.

Loading 'foreach' in windows (RStudio) was not possible.

I checked the dependencies of 'foreach' and find that the dependency 'doMC' is not available for windows (though it is there in CRAN packages).

Is there a way to work around this or windows users cannot use INLA at the moment?

Any pointers will be greatly appreciated.

Thank you.

Danlin Yu

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] I am not able to Load INLA package because the foreach and doMC packages cannot be installed/loaded. Help
parts:
Hi, make sure you’re using R-4.0 and then you need to install the testing version of INLA. Just replace /stable with /testing in the path.


-- 
Håvard Rue

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] I am not able to Load INLA package because the foreach and doMC packages cannot be installed/loaded. Help
parts:
Thank you, Dr. Håvard Rue:

I was using the testing version of INLA with R-4.02, but having the same problem.

I traced back all the potential dependencies and found that once I installed 'doMC' package from the .zip file, and installed the package 'iterators', everything works out fine.

I just hope next time when I update everything, it will work out as well.

Thank you for your response and contribution. I am enjoying the package very much.

Best,

Danlin Yu

parts:
This happens when I was trying to load INLA (library(INLA)), and it will
report that package 'foreach' cannot be loaded, which turned out to be
depending on the package 'doMC' and 'iterators'. I installed both and it
worked out fine (I guess on retrospective, installing 'iterators'
probably will work, too). I did re-install everything after upgrade to
R-4.0.

Thank you for your support.

Best,

Danlin
